entries.title: Stellar lifetime desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a stellar-lifetime page. Mass runs from 0.1 to 60 solar masses on a log slider. Inside 0.179 < M ≤ 31, luminosity is the six-piece fit of Eker et al. 2018, Table 4: log10(L/L☉) = a log10(M/M☉) + b. The pieces are separate lines. They are not joined, and they are not used outside that window. At 1 M☉ the low-mass line gives log L = −0.007, about 0.984 L☉, not 1. Main-sequence lifetime is t ≈ 10 Gyr × M/L. With the IAU nominal L = 1 the Sun is exactly 10 Gyr. With the fit it is about 10.16 Gyr. The 10 Gyr zero is the classroom round number beside NASA’s 4.6-billion-year-old Sun plus about 5 billion years still on the main sequence (sum 9.6). It is not a model age. End-state labels follow NASA Science: under 8 M☉ a white dwarf, about 8 to 20 a neutron star, heavier a black hole. Heger et al. 2003 move those edges with metallicity, rotation, and mass loss. The plot marks the Planck 2018 age from Table 2, column TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing: 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr. The +BAO column is 13.787 ± 0.020 Gyr. Cited presets: Proxima Centauri 0.120 ± 0.003 M☉ and 0.00151 ± 0.00008 L☉ (Ribas et al. 2017; below the fit; 10 × 0.120 / 0.00151 is about 795 Gyr), Sirius A 2.063 ± 0.023 M☉ and 24.74 ± 0.70 L☉ (Bond et al. 2017; about 834 Myr; YREC age 237 ± 15 Myr), Vega mass 2.15 M☉ with +0.10 and −0.15 (Monnier et al. 2012) and 44 ± 2 L☉ (Hill, Gulliver, and Adelman 2010; about 489 Myr, shorter than the cited 700 Myr age), Rigel log(L/L☉) = 5.08 and a track mass of 23 M☉ (Moravveji et al. 2012). Rigel is a blue supergiant, so the fit at 23 M☉ is not its present luminosity. Formula outputs are approximate scaling estimates. Not a stellar-evolution model.

entries.title: Telescope optics desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a telescope-optics page. Focal ratio is focal length over aperture. Magnification is telescope focal length over eyepiece focal length, and a Barlow multiplies that effective focal length. Exit pupil is aperture over magnification. The rough true field is apparent field divided by magnification. Light grasp compares the aperture with a 7 mm pupil, the traditional maximum Sky & Telescope states. Rayleigh’s criterion is 1.22 λ/D. Dawes’s empirical limit is printed as 116/D in millimetres and as 4.56/D in inches. A classroom 200 mm f/6 with a 25 mm eyepiece and a 50° apparent field is 48×, exit pupil 4.17 mm, true field 1.042° (62.5′), light grasp 816×, Rayleigh 0.692″ at 550 nm, and Dawes 0.580″ (116/D) and 0.579″ (4.56/D). At naked-eye magnitude 6.0 the collecting-area estimate is 13.28. Bowen’s 1947 formula gives 12.94. Hubble uses the STScI primer’s 2.4 m aperture at f/24, focal length 57.6 m. JWST uses NASA’s 6.5 m and 131.4 m, which compute to f/20.22. The 7×50, 80 mm, and 200 mm sets are round classroom numbers, not catalog models. Not a buying guide.

entries.title: Habitable zone desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a habitable-zone page: stellar flux S/S⊕ = (L/L☉)/d², and watts per square metre from the NASA Earth Fact Sheet solar irradiance, 1361.0 W/m². Equilibrium temperature assumes full heat redistribution and emissivity 1: T_eq = [F(1−A)/(4σ)]¼. Earth’s Bond albedo 0.294 at 1 AU gives S/S⊕ = 1.000 and T_eq = 255.1 K. The fact sheet’s average surface temperature is 288 K. The strip is Kopparapu et al. 2014, conservative and optimistic, 1 Earth mass, valid from 2600 K to 7200 K and not drawn outside that range. Presets: Venus, Earth, and Mars from the NASA fact sheets; Proxima Centauri b (Ribas et al. 2017; Anglada-Escudé et al. 2016); TRAPPIST-1 e (Agol et al. 2021), whose 2566 K host is below the polynomial; Kepler-452b (Jenkins et al. 2015). A point in the strip is not a habitability verdict.

entries.title: Transit and radial-velocity desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a transit page: depth δ ≈ (Rp/R*)², geometric probability about R*/a, a circular-orbit duration, and radial-velocity semi-amplitude K with m sin i. Masses are fact-sheet GM ratios, so G is not chosen. Earth–Sun, volumetric mean radii and i = 90°, is 83.86 ppm and 8.95 cm/s. Jupiter–Sun is 1.010% and 12.46 m/s. Cited presets: HD 209458 b (Bonomo et al. 2017), 51 Pegasi b (Cont et al. 2026; no planet radius, because the archive flags the composite radius as calculated), TRAPPIST-1 e (Agol et al. 2021), and GJ 1214 b (Mahajan, Eastman, and Kirk 2024). Uniform disk, no limb darkening, no eccentricity. Not a catalog and not a fitted light curve.

entries.title: HR diagram desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Hertzsprung–Russell page: effective temperature across, hot on the left, and luminosity L/L☉ up. Radius lines are L = 4πR²σT⁴. σ is the CODATA value 5.670374419… × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. The zero is the IAU 2015 nominal Sun, 5772 K and 1 R☉, and the bolometric magnitude uses M_bol,☉ = 4.74. Cited central values: Proxima 2980 ± 80 K and 0.00151 ± 0.00008 L☉ (Ribas et al. 2017), Vega 9560 ± 30 K and 44 ± 2 L☉ (Hill, Gulliver, and Adelman 2010), Sirius A 9845 ± 64 K and 24.74 ± 0.70 L☉, Sirius B 25,369 ± 46 K and 0.02448 ± 0.00033 L☉ (Bond et al. 2017), Betelgeuse log(L/L☉) = 5.10 ± 0.22 (Dolan et al. 2016), Rigel log(L/L☉) = 5.08 (Moravveji et al. 2012). The Sun’s visual absolute magnitude +4.83 stays the fact-sheet figure, not the bolometric 4.74. Main sequence, giants, and white dwarfs are a classroom cartoon. Not a Gaia catalog and not an ephemeris.

entries.title: Redshift desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a redshift page: z = (λ_obs − λ_rest)/λ_rest. At z = 1 the special-relativistic Doppler formula gives β = 0.6, while c·z equals the speed of light and is not a speed. Cosmological redshift is 1+z = a_now/a_then. The nearby Hubble toy is v = H0·d, with Planck 2018 H0 = 67.4 ± 0.5 km/s/Mpc and SH0ES 2022 H0 = 73.04 ± 1.04 km/s/Mpc. At a classroom 10 Mpc those central values are 674 km/s and 730.4 km/s. Cited presets: Andromeda z = −0.001 (SIMBAD), NGC 4258 z = 0.00158 (BASS DR2), 3C 273 z = 0.15756751 (SIMBAD), GN-z11 z = 10.6034 (Bunker et al. 2023). Rest wavelengths are NIST: Lyα 121.567 nm vacuum, Ca II K 393.36614 nm air, Ca II H 396.84673 nm air, Hβ 486.132 nm air, Hα 656.280 nm air. The visible shade is the NASA Imagine classroom window, 400–700 nm. Not a catalog spectrum and not a distance to those objects.

entries.title: Blackbody desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a blackbody page: Planck’s curve B_λ(T), Wien’s peak λ_max = b/T, and luminosity L = 4πR²σT⁴. b is the CODATA constant 2.897771955… × 10⁻³ m·K. σ is 5.670374419… × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. The comparison Sun is the IAU 2015 nominal effective temperature, 5772 K, and the nominal solar radius. The visible shade is the NASA Imagine classroom window, 400–700 nm. The nominal Sun peaks near 502 nm and the chip is still warm white, not green. Presets use cited central values: Proxima 2980 ± 80 K and 0.146 ± 0.007 R☉ (Ribas et al. 2017), Vega’s mean 9560 ± 30 K and equatorial 2.75 ± 0.01 R☉ (Hill, Gulliver, and Adelman 2010; the star is oblate), Rigel 12,100 ± 150 K and 78.9 ± 7.4 R☉ (Moravveji et al. 2012), Betelgeuse 3500 ± 200 K and 887 ± 203 R☉ (Dolan et al. 2016). The color chip is an sRGB approximation. Real spectra have absorption lines. The science hub also gains cards for the astronomy desks it had been missing.

entries.title: Twilight desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a twilight page: sunrise, sunset, and the three twilights, from NOAA’s solar calculator in the browser. Astronomical dawn is the Sun 18° below the horizon, nautical 12°, civil 6°, and sunrise is the standard −0.833° (about 34′ of refraction plus about 16′ of solar semi-diameter). For Campbell on 21 June 2024 the desk reads sunrise 05:48 PDT and sunset 20:32 PDT, matching the U.S. Naval Observatory to the minute. Golden hour and blue hour are approximate altitude bands. Polar day, polar night, and twilight all night are labeled. A year chart shows how day length and twilight change with latitude.

entries.title: Magnitude desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a magnitude page: apparent magnitude m, absolute magnitude M, and the distance modulus m − M = 5 log10(d / 10 pc). Five magnitudes is a flux ratio of 100, because 10^(0.4·5) = 100. At 10 pc, m = M. The Sun’s fact-sheet absolute magnitude is +4.83, so from there it would look like magnitude +4.83. At 1 AU the same formula gives −26.742, which rounds to the sheet’s visual magnitude −26.74. Extinction is ignored. Visual (V) band. Not a catalog.

entries.title: C3 desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a characteristic-energy page: C3 = v∞² = 2ε for a hyperbolic departure from a circular parking orbit. Earth’s GM and volumetric radius are the fact sheet’s. At 400 km, a classroom altitude the sheet does not print, circular speed is 7.673 km/s and local escape is 10.851 km/s, so C3 = 0 is a 3.178 km/s burn. A classroom v∞ of 3 km/s is C3 = 9 km²/s², periapsis speed 11.258 km/s, and a 3.585 km/s burn. The same C3 on the geosynchronous classroom circle costs 2.208 km/s. The lower circle costs more because it starts deeper in the well. At a classroom 450 s the 3.178 km/s burn leaves mf/m0 = 0.4867. Ideal, impulsive, no atmosphere. Not a mission.

entries.title: Rocket desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a rocket-equation page: Δv = ve · ln(m0/mf), with ve = Isp · g0 and g0 = 9.80665 m/s². Ideal rocket, constant exhaust speed, no gravity losses and no drag. The Oberth desk’s 3.178 km/s escape burn from a 400 km classroom circle, at a classroom 450 s, leaves mf/m0 = 0.4867. The Hohmann desk’s Earth-to-Mars 5.594 km/s, at the same 450 s, leaves 0.2815. At a classroom 300 s those remaining fractions are 0.3395 and 0.1494. The 300 s and 450 s figures are classroom examples, not engine datasheets. Not a mission planner.

entries.title: Gravity assist desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a gravity-assist page: in the planet frame a flyby is an unpowered hyperbola, e = 1 + r_p v∞²/μ, and the turn is δ = 2 arcsin(1/e). The planet keeps moving. Earth’s classroom 5 km/s pass, 400 km above the volumetric radius, turns 89.16°. Heliocentric speed goes from 26.515 km/s to 33.484 km/s. The assist magnitude is 7.019 km/s. At the same excess and the same periapsis ratio, Jupiter turns 160.50° and Mars turns 37.60°. Fact-sheet GM. The 5 km/s excess is a classroom example. Not a mission planner.

entries.title: Oberth desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows an Oberth page: the same impulsive Δv changes specific orbital energy by v·Δv + ½(Δv)². From a classroom circle 400 km up, with Earth’s GM, circular speed is 7.673 km/s, local escape is 10.851 km/s, and Δv to escape is 3.178 km/s. A 1 km/s burn gains 8.173 km²/s² there and 3.575 km²/s² on a classroom circle at the geosynchronous radius, 42,164.190 km. A 6 km/s burn leaves 8.319 km/s at infinity from the low circle and 7.965 km/s from the higher one. Point-mass, impulsive. Not a mission.

entries.title: Vis-viva desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a vis-viva page: speed anywhere on a Keplerian ellipse, v = √[μ (2/r − 1/a)]. Earth’s printed perihelion, with the Sun’s GM, is 30.287 km/s. The Earth Fact Sheet lists 30.29 km/s. Aphelion is 29.291 km/s; the sheet lists 29.29 km/s. The Moon, Mars, a 400 km circular orbit, and a schematic ellipse with e = 0.5 sit beside it. Point-mass, two-body. Not an ephemeris.

entries.title: Angular size desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows an angular-size page: δ = 2·arctan(d / 2D), with the small-angle d/D in radians beside the exact angle. The Moon’s volumetric mean diameter is 3,474.8 km. Mean perigee, 0.3633 × 10⁶ km, is 32.880′. Mean apogee is 29.458′. The perigee disc is 11.616% wider. The Sun’s diameter is 1,391,400 km. Perihelion is 32.518′ and aphelion is 31.448′. Perigee Moon over perihelion Sun is 1.0111, enough to cover. Apogee Moon over perihelion Sun is 0.9059, a ring. Fact-sheet radii and distances. Thumb, coin, and a 5 mm mark are approximate. Schematic, not an ephemeris.

entries.title: Hill desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Hill page: the sphere around a secondary where that body dominates a test particle. The classroom form is r_H ≈ a (m/(3M))^(1/3), with the μ form beside it, the same approximation the Lagrange desk uses for L1 and L2. Sun–Earth is 1,496,565 km. The Moon at 384,400 km sits inside. Jupiter’s sphere is 53,147,220 km. Phobos at 9,378 km is deep inside Mars’s sphere, and still between the Roche limits. Fact-sheet masses and orbits. Schematic, not an ephemeris.

entries.title: Orrery speed
entries.blurb: The solar map speed control is a logarithmic slider from 1 hour per second to 10 years per second. The readout is the rate, such as 12.3 days/s. Arrow keys take a fine step; Shift is coarser. Minus, plus, and a number field sit beside it. The 0.5×–10× presets, pause, and Now stay. The same clock drives the 3D orrery and the 2D map.

entries.title: Circuit maker
entries.blurb: The circuit explorer keeps its eighteen lessons and gains a maker. Place resistors, pots, capacitors, inductors, switches, diodes, LEDs, an NPN, an op-amp, logic gates, and a 555. Wires snap on a grid. A modified-nodal solver shows the DC point, then a transient scope. Probe and meter, rotate and flip, undo, copy, zoom. Shorts, floating nodes, and an LED past 20 mA are called out. Save a JSON file, or a link, and it also stays in this browser. Educational models, not a bench supply.

entries.title: ASL trainer
entries.blurb: Languages gains an ASL trainer: original diagrams for the fingerspelling alphabet, numbers 0–20, and a starter vocabulary. Learn, Leitner flashcards, recognition and recall quizzes, a fingerspelling reader, and a spell-it practice. J and Z, and the signs that move, use arrows or numbered frames. Progress stays in this browser, with save and load to a text file. The drawings are simplified. A beginner aid, not a class, and not a substitute for Deaf instructors.

entries.title: 3D solar map
entries.blurb: The solar system map opens in 3D. The eight planets use NASA JPL approximate Keplerian elements, eccentricity and inclination included. Pluto and a few major moons are optional. Drag to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom, and switch Compressed or True AU. Sizes stay exaggerated. The flat map, with day, local time, play, and speed, is still the 2D control. Schematic, not a Horizons ephemeris.

entries.title: Roche desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Roche page: the distance inside which a moon cannot hold together. The fluid limit is 2.44 primary radii times the cube root of the density ratio. The rigid limit uses 1.26. Saturn–Rhea, Earth–Moon, and Mars–Phobos use NASA fact-sheet mean densities, mean radii, and mean orbits. Rhea and the Moon sit outside both limits. Phobos sits between them. A density-ratio slider moves the two arcs. Saturn’s A-ring outer edge, 136,780 km, sits inside the equal-density fluid distance. Schematic, not an ephemeris.

entries.title: Lagrange desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Lagrange page: five equilibrium points of a two-body system, drawn in the rotating frame. Sun–Earth, Earth–Moon, and Sun–Jupiter, from fact-sheet masses and semimajor axes. The Hill approximation sits beside a numerical collinear root. Sun–Earth L1 is 1,491,557 km from Earth and L2 is 1,501,538 km. Earth–Moon L1 is 326,380 km from Earth and 58,020 km from the Moon. L4 and L5 are 60° ahead and behind. Circular, coplanar, a massless third body. Not a mission.

entries.title: Tenant issues
entries.blurb: Tools gains a tenant-issues page: a log for maintenance and habitability problems, kept until they are resolved or closed. Each issue holds a room, a category, a priority, work order numbers, when it was noticed and reported, how it was reported, who was contacted, and a follow-up date. A dated note can record a new status, so the history stays with the issue. The list filters by status, searches, sorts, counts each status, and marks days open and overdue follow-ups. Save downloads a plain text file; Load reads that file back. The browser keeps a copy too. Nothing is uploaded. An organizing record, not legal advice.

entries.title: Hohmann desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Hohmann page: two circular orbits and the half-ellipse tangent to both, Sun at the focus. Earth to Mars, from the fact-sheet kilometer semimajor axes and the Sun’s GM, takes 258.88 days and 5.594 km/s. Mars must lead by 44.34°. Scrub the coast, or try Venus, Jupiter, or a classroom low orbit around Earth. Circular, coplanar, impulsive. Not a mission.

entries.title: Escape desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows an escape-speed page: pick a world and an altitude, and read circular orbital speed and escape speed at that radius. They stay a factor of √2 apart. Earth’s fact-sheet GM and volumetric mean radius, 6,371.000 km, give 11.186 km/s at the surface, the figure the Earth Fact Sheet lists. A sideways launch draws the fall, the circle, the ellipse, and the open escape curve. The Gravity desk names Newton’s cannon and does not compute these speeds. Schematic, no air and no spin, not a trajectory.

entries.title: Kepler desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Kepler page: a top-down Sun and one circular orbit. Drag the semi-major axis from Mercury to Neptune. In classroom units, P² = a³ when P is in years and a is in AU. Presets use each fact sheet’s Semimajor axis (AU) and sidereal orbit period. Earth’s sheet prints 1.00000011 AU and 365.256 days. Play is a time-lapse. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not a trajectory.

entries.title: Libration desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a libration page: a north-up Moon globe with the mean Earth-facing hemisphere marked. The fact sheet’s spin, 655.720 hours, matches the 27.3217-day orbit. Eccentricity 0.0549 peeks past the east and west limbs. The equator is tilted 6.68° to the orbit, so the nod peeks past the poles. A JPL note says geometric libration makes 59% of the surface visible over time. The peek on the drawing is exaggerated. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not tonight’s Moon.

entries.title: Precession desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a precession page: a tilted Earth and a slow circle of the north celestial pole. Polaris now, Thuban in 3000 B.C., Vega in about 13,000 years, on a classroom loop of about 26,000 years. Obliquity stays 23.44°. The tropical year is 365.242 days and the sidereal year is 365.256. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not astrology.

entries.title: Synodic month desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a synodic-month page: a top-down Sun, Earth on a short arc, and the Moon. One trip against the stars is 27.3217 days; new Moon to new Moon is 29.53. The Moon is back among the stars and the Sun has moved on, so the same phase is still ahead. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not a phase calendar.

entries.title: Sidereal day desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a sidereal page: a top-down Sun, a spinning Earth, and a fixed star. One turn against the star is 23.9345 hours; the mean solar day is 24.0000. The mark still has a little farther to turn before the Sun is back, which is why the stars rise about four minutes earlier. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not a clock for navigation.

entries.title: How to test a computer power supply
entries.blurb: A beginner’s bench test with a multimeter: the 24-pin plug from the wire side, the other desktop plugs, and the Intel voltage windows. Colored plugs only. Never open the case.

entries.title: Kundali matching
entries.blurb: Chakras gains an Ashtakoota desk: 36 guna points from two birth times and places, or from Moon nakshatras you already know. Lahiri ayanamsa, in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Planet phases
entries.blurb: Astronomy adds phase desks for Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, beside Venus. Inferior planets run crescent to full. Superior planets stay gibbous to full — the minimum lit fraction is computed from the fact-sheet orbit ratio. Jupiter adds a spacecraft observer: drag it outside Earth’s wedge and the disk can crescent, the view Voyager, Cassini, and Juno recorded and Earth cannot. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris.

entries.title: Daily wallpapers
entries.blurb: Wallpapers reads one manifest. The newest image marked daily is Today's wallpaper — or the newest image, if none is marked. Nature and Sci-fi collections share that list and filter in the archive, newest first, same-day order kept. Drop in a file and one entry. Every image is generated with Grok Imagine.

entries.title: The ice crop
entries.blurb: A history of harvesting ice, from Mari and the Zhou ice pits through Tudor, Norway, and Chimborazo, with a timeline. Commercial ice came from lakes, rivers, and mountain glaciers. People did not mine tons of ice at the poles and ship them. Cited.

entries.title: Opposition desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows an opposition page: a top-down Sun, Earth, and Mars on circular orbits. Play or scrub one schematic synodic lap — opposition, quadrature, conjunction — and the angle at Earth shows why an outer planet stands opposite the Sun or gets lost near it. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not a finder chart.

entries.title: Venus phases desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Venus page: a top-down Sun, Venus, and Earth on circular orbits. Play or scrub from a schematic inferior conjunction and the disk runs crescent through gibbous — evening star, morning star, and the far-side near-full. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not a finder chart.

entries.title: Retrograde desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a retrograde page: a top-down Sun, Earth, and Mars on circular orbits. Play or scrub and Earth laps the outer planet. A line of sight and a longitude strip show the backward loop — prograde, stationary, retrograde — while both orbit arrows keep going the same way. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not for pointing a telescope.

entries.title: No Man's Sky moodboard
entries.blurb: The material graph is now three desks. The moodboard is a dense grid — minerals, gases, plants, earth, and early components. Click to open, mark several, and star a short list that stays in this browser. Refine stays the edge explorer. The planner is a stub that reads those pins. Craft rows are station inventory. High-speed sublimation is the three-slot path to nitrogen salt, enriched carbon, and thermic condensate. Wiring loom stays buy-only. Community ratios — a patch can change a recipe.

entries.title: Game guides — No Man's Sky bases
entries.blurb: Game guides opens at /game/guides/, separate from the playable /games/ pages. First tool: a No Man's Sky base map. Load exported JSON or a Steam save.hg in the browser, plot planetary bases on a schematic disk, and mark the Euclid Hub capital at Uthmi Beta. Zoom toward the pointer or the selected base; same-system piles spread apart and show their names. Freighter bases stay listed aside. Nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Tides desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a tides page: a top-down Earth with exaggerated ocean bulges. Slide the Moon from new to full and the label switches from spring to neap. A light spin shows two highs per turn under bulges that stay put. Cited NASA and NOAA. Schematic, not a tide table — and not a Campbell harbor guide.

entries.title: Eclipses desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows an eclipses page: a side-view Sun, Earth, and Moon on a tilted orbit. Toggle solar or lunar, then slide the node offset from aligned to about 5° and watch the shadow miss. Umbra, penumbra, nodes, eclipse seasons. Cited NASA. Schematic, not a prediction.

entries.title: Seasons day length
entries.blurb: The seasons desk adds day length by latitude — a slider from pole to pole, tied to the same day-of-year control. Near equinox the strip stays near 12 hours; solstice stretches toward the poles. Classroom hour-angle math, not a sunrise almanac.

entries.title: Seasons desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a seasons page: walk the year, keep Earth’s axis parallel at about 23.4°, and see which hemisphere leans into the Sun. Perihelion is early January — Northern winter. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris or a forecast.

entries.title: Humanoid robots status essay
entries.blurb: Science robotics grows a nested 2025–2026 stand: Figure Helix 2.5 in unseen homes, electric Atlas and Digit 5 on industrial floors, Optimus production talk labeled as plans. Cited. Company claims and supply-chain reports can outrun verified deployments.

entries.title: Weather wind direction
entries.blurb: The weather desk now shows wind direction with speed — compass point and degrees from Open-Meteo (direction the wind blows from).

entries.title: Electromagnetic spectrum desk
entries.blurb: Science grows a radio-to-gamma literacy page: tap the bands for classroom wavelength and frequency ranges, then slide a Wien’s-law peak (Sun ~5800 K near visible). Cited NASA / Imagine the Universe. Not a lab instrument or medical advice.

entries.title: Text tools desk
entries.blurb: Tools grows a character counter with live words/lines/UTF-8 bytes, case convert, trim, sort, dedupe, copy, and download. Runs in the browser — nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Wallpapers desk
entries.blurb: Free desktop wallpapers with in-browser cover-crop downloads — original, common sizes, and custom W×H. First image: Pacific Northwest Coast at Golden Hour (Grok Imagine / AI-generated; native 1792×1008, larger sizes labeled upscales).

entries.title: Annual Dial text backup
entries.blurb: Save day marks from the Annual Dial as a readable .txt, then restore that file — replace or merge — so entries survive a cleared browser and can move between devices. Local only; nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Standard Model desk
entries.blurb: Science grows a particle-physics literacy page: clickable quark / lepton / boson grid, generations, force diagram, and honest gaps (gravity, dark matter, neutrino mass). Cited CERN / Fermilab / PDG. Not a QFT course.

entries.title: Gravity desk
entries.blurb: Science grows a sibling literacy page for the force the Standard Model omits: everyday weight and orbits, Newton, Einstein / GPS, weakness vs other forces, and the quantum-gravity gap. Cited NASA / NIST / CERN. Not a theory of everything.

entries.title: Internet speed test
entries.blurb: Tools desk grows a browser speed test — ping, download, and upload against Cloudflare’s public edge. Approximate. Not a lab meter. Not affiliated with Cloudflare or Ookla.

entries.title: Solar map play speed
entries.blurb: Play on the solar system map now has a speed control — 0.5× through 10×, labeled in days per second. Date and local time stay the source of truth; share still uses ?date= and ?time=.

entries.title: Solar map day & time
entries.blurb: The solar system map now takes a local day and time — planets sit at approximate mean heliocentric longitudes for that moment. Schematic, not a JPL ephemeris. Share with ?date= and ?time=.

entries.title: Stars types & lives
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a color lesson: clickable OBAFGKM strip, steppable life-phase timeline (Sun-like and high-mass), and an HR cartoon with Sun, Vega, Sirius, Betelgeuse, Proxima. Cited NASA/textbook ranges. Not a research tool.

entries.title: Local sky city or ZIP
entries.blurb: The local sky chart now takes a city name or US ZIP — same Open-Meteo geocoding as weather — so the viewpoint, LST, and horizon follow you. Defaults to Campbell.

entries.title: Day for Night on Salesforce Tower
entries.blurb: Nested light-pollution essay: Jim Campbell’s civic diary on the 1,070-ft crown, inward-facing LEDs vs Times Square, skyglow literacy, and South Bay / Peninsula unease. Cited. Not a hit piece.

entries.title: South Bay education quality
